key_insight: Visual Attribution Distillation (VAD) separates true visual evidence from mixed correction signals in multimodal on-policy distillation. This lets the student learn from what the teacher can actually see, instead of also inheriting linguistic priors or teacher-specific artifacts.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a core OPD challenge: next-token corrections are "source-mixed," meaning they blend visual information with language priors and teacher behavior. The goal is to identify which corrections are genuinely supported by visual evidence for target reconstruction.
method: Uses counterfactual target reconstruction to estimate whether a correction is attributable to visual evidence.
Focuses on attribution, not just correction magnitude, to distinguish visual signals from non-visual confounds.
Applies this attribution to guide distillation so the student receives cleaner, more faithful supervision.
impact: For practitioners, VAD offers a more reliable way to transfer visual knowledge in multimodal models, improving supervision quality in settings where teacher outputs are noisy or biased. This can lead to better student performance and more interpretable distillation.

paper_title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Kangning Zhang, Yixing Li, Shuai Shao, Qingyao Li, Zhengxi Lu
